ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows a grounded left-middle node. A vertical 13 V source connects this ground node to the upper-left node, then a 6Ω resistor leads to node x. Node x also connects downward through a 5Ω resistor to a lower-left node l, which connects through a 2Ω resistor back to ground. From node x to the right there is a 5 V source, then a 3Ω resistor to a top-middle node t. Node t connects right through a 4Ω resistor to a top-right node r, which goes downward through a 2Ω resistor to point A. Node t also connects downward through a vertical 3Ω resistor to the top node p of a 17 V source; the lower node q of that 17 V source connects through an 8Ω resistor to point A. Reasoning: Take the grounded left-middle node as 0 V. Using the source polarities specified in the method: the upper terminal of the 13 V source is U = 13 V; the node y to the right of the 5 V source satisfies y = x - 5; and the node q below the 17 V source satisfies q = p - 17. KCL for the supernode around the 5 V source is (x - 13)/6 + (x - l)/5 + (y - t)/3 = 0. KCL at lower-left node l is (l - x)/5 + l/2 = 0, giving l = 2x/7. Substituting y = x - 5 and l = 2x/7 into the 5 V supernode equation gives 27x - 14t - 161 = 0, so x = (14t + 161)/27 and y = x - 5 = (14t + 26)/27. On the right side, KCL at node r gives (r - t)/4 + (r - A)/2 = 0, so r = (t + 2A)/3. KCL at point A gives (A - r)/2 + (A - q)/8 = 0, so q = 5A - 4r. KCL for the supernode around the 17 V source gives (p - t)/3 + (q - A)/8 = 0 with q = p - 17. Solving these right-side relations gives A = t - 6, r = t - 4, q = t - 14, and p = t + 3. Finally, KCL at top-middle node t is (t - y)/3 + (t - r)/4 + (t - p)/3 = 0. Since r = t - 4 and p = t + 3, the last two terms are +1 and -1, so they cancel and t = y. Therefore t = (14t + 26)/27, giving 27t = 14t + 26, so 13t = 26 and t = 2 V. Hence A = t - 6 = -4 V.

Solve the simultaneous linear equations for the node voltage at A relative to ground; the solution gives VA = -4 V.
